latin: Peccatum Adae fuit truncatio regni a caeteris plantis.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch10, from Latin at farmer1998:17598
translation: The sin of Adam was the severing of the kingdom from the rest of the shoots.
translation_note: Rendered directly from the Latin at farmer1998:17544, checked against Farmer's sense at farmer1998:17598.
latin_note: Farmer's apparatus records a variant reading, 'coetens', in the 1486 print at this point in the text, without identifying which word of the 1487/copy-text reading it replaces (farmer1998:17555).

sources.text: the Zohar and Menahem Recanati's commentary (as cited via Scholem and Wirszubski)
sources.pico_relation: Farmer's note traces the 'severing of the shoots' image, here applied to Adam's sin, to this common kabbalistic association of the sefirot with the tree of paradise

doctrine: The thesis reads Adam's sin kabbalistically, as the severing of 'the kingdom' — the tenth sefirah — from the other 'shoots', the higher sefirot figured as a tree, a standard symbol for the origin of sin found in the Zohar and in Recanati (farmer1998:17617). Farmer directs the reader to Scholem and to Wirszubski's own discussion of the same image (farmer1998:17617).
historiography: Wirszubski identifies this as the fourth conclusion of Pico's Cabalistic set and quotes it twice in his discussion of its background (wirszubski1989:1390, 1393).

quotations.text: CONCLUSIO IV Peccatum Adae fuit truncatio regni a caeteris plantis.

not_established: A further Wirszubski record found under the same search (wirszubski1989:9972) quotes a differently numbered 'Conclusio iv', on the correspondence of David's and Orpheus's hymns to the Cabala and to magic; that record concerns a different thesis of Pico's, its own Farmer id is not resolved in the packet, and it is not used in this entry.
